questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a major leak
A valve that prevents the truck from being stolen
A valve that prevents the driver from going too fast
A valve that prevents the trailer from accidentally disconnecting

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a major leak
questions.explanation: On trucks with air brakes, the tractor protection valve saves air in the truck's brake system if the trailer disconnects or develops a leak.

questions.question: Trailers made before ____ do not need spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers made before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to stop it from rolling.

questions.question: When backing up your tractor to couple it to a trailer, the trailer brakes should be:

options.text: Turned off
Locked
Unlocked

questions.explanation: To safely couple and uncouple trailers, follow the correct steps. Before backing your tractor under the trailer, lock the trailer brakes.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should:

options.text: Be used for parking
Be used only to test the trailer brakes
Be used with the brake pedal
Be used on slippery roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used only to test the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve controls the trailer brakes but should only be used for testing them. Using it while driving can cause a skid. Never use it for parking because it may release air pressure and let the brakes fail.

questions.question: If you are driving a vehicle made before 1998 and are not sure if the trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you can:

options.text: Look for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly
Pump the air brakes to turn on the ABS
Assume the vehicle has ABS

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes
questions.explanation: If you are driving a vehicle made before 1998 and are not sure if the trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To test the trailer brakes
To check if the trailer and tractor are connected
To speed up

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the "trolley valve" or "Johnson bar") controls the trailer brakes and should only be used for testing. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: When coupling:

options.text: You can assume all vehicles are the same
Make sure you couple correctly
Cracks in the mounting are okay

questions.explanation: Incorrect coupling and uncoupling of combination vehicles can be very dangerous.

questions.question: If you use the trailer hand brake while your trailer is skidding, it will:

options.text: Stop the skid
Straighten the trailer
Keep the skid going

questions.explanation: If your trailer starts to skid, you can help your tires grip the road by releasing the brakes. Using the trailer hand brake during a skid will only make it worse.

questions.question: When glad hands are connected, the seals should be pressed together at what angle:

options.text: 30 degrees
45 degrees
60 degrees
90 degrees

questions.explanation: When coupling, connect the correct glad hands. The seals should be pressed together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be:

options.text: A little higher than the center of the fifth wheel
Level with the center of the fifth wheel
A little lower than the center of the fifth wheel
Next to the center of the fifth wheel

questions.correctAnswerText: A little lower than the center of the fifth wheel
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height must be correct. It should be a little lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: How can you check if a vehicle built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Pump the air brakes to turn on the ABS.
Look inside the back of the fifth wheel.
Look for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a vehicle built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What does the tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Protects the tractor from being stolen.
Prevents the tractor from going too fast.
Keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks loose or leaks.
Makes sure oil lubricates the engine properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks loose or leaks.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks loose or develops a leak.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high?

options.text: It will not make a difference when coupling.
It may not couple correctly.
Coupling will be more secure.
Coupling will be easier.

questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, make sure the trailer is at the right height. If the trailer is too low, the nose may get damaged. If the trailer is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Stop air from escaping the brake system.
Stop air from entering the brake system.
Control vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from escaping the brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow in brake lines between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to prevent air from leaving the brake system.

questions.question: When should a trolley valve be used?

options.text: While driving.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
When parking uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause the vehicle to skid. Do not use it while parking because it may release air pressure and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: What happens when a combination vehicle turns a corner?

options.text: The vehicle must use at least two lanes.
The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
It is best to let the rear wheels drive over the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. This effect is more noticeable on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: How can a driver prevent a rollover?

options.text: Keep cargo low.
Place cargo high.
Keep cargo loose.
Turn quickly.

questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a combination vehicle turns too quickly. To prevent rollovers, keep the center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: Which trailer is most likely to roll over if a driver turns too quickly?

options.text: The front trailer.
The last trailer.
The middle trailer.

questions.explanation: When turning, steer gently and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous and increase the risk of the last trailer rolling over.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, what is especially important?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you into their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. When entering or crossing traffic, make sure there is a large enough gap for you to safely enter.

questions.question: What causes more than half of all truck driver deaths from accidents?

options.text: Truck rollovers.
Motorcycles.
Slippery roads.
Pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of all truck driver deaths from accidents. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered on your vehicle. Take corners slowly and carefully.
